The 3D example's island is a 3D level, made once from noise by makeLevel: a terrain block of 129 samples, its height colors as paint from a list of 23, and Tree (level3DAddMesh), Sprite, Orb and PlayerStart objects, 163 trees, 32 sprites and 40 orbs where 1000 trees and 150 sprites were scattered before; loadLevel builds it and is the editor's Restart, with the lights, the flare and the title persistent; Esc then 0 opens the 3D editor on it, where before the 2D editor opened with nothing to edit and the view stood still; levelFile loads a saved level3D.json in place of the noise; the game's hint is hidden while the editor is open; its write-up says so

TcpStack: a stopping listener leaves its slot only if it still holds it (RemoveListener: by key and value; the wildcard slot only if it is this listener), where an old listener's Stop, racing a Listen after StopListening took it out, removed the replacement; a test keeps the replacement registered and accepting (a third-party review's finding)

TcpStack: a ListenAny or Listen that Dispose overtakes throws, where it published a listener the disposed stack never closed: ListenAny checks under the lock Dispose takes after setting its flag, and Listen re-checks after its add and stops the listener; a test holds ListenAny at the lock while Dispose runs (a third-party review's finding, with its twin in Listen)

TcpStack: a segment of a tracked tuple goes to its connection first, so a SYN there draws a challenge ACK and its data is dropped (RFC 9293 3.10.7.4, RFC 5961 4), a bare SYN in SYN-RECEIVED the SYN-ACK again, and a SYN with RST is a RST; where a SYN+ACK passed as a data segment and could complete a handshake, and a SYN+RST to an unknown tuple opened a connection; a test for each (a third-party review's finding)

TcpStack: MaxConnections holds under concurrent SYNs: the slot is reserved by compare-and-swap before the connection is made and given back if it is not, where the count was checked first and raised after; the peak counts admitted connections only; a test races 16 SYNs at a cap of 1 (a third-party review's finding)

TcpStack: a fast retransmission restarts the RTO, which must not resend the segment within an RTO of it (RFC 6298 5), where the RTO fired at the original send's deadline, moments after the fast one; a test times the RTO's copy (a third-party review's finding)

Packets: a TCP packet whose data offset is below the 20-byte header or past the packet's end is rejected at parse, where Payload handed the header's bytes on as data - one shift and two compares per parse; a test feeds the stack a 16-byte header (a third-party review's finding)

TcpStack: a read after the stream's end returns 0 again, where it threw "Reading is already in progress": the end's empty read left the pipe's read open; a test reads past the end twice (a third-party review's finding)
